KEY MESSAGE 1...
A cold front crossing the area early this morning will exit to
the southeast by sunrise. Chilly northwest flow is supporting 
lake effect clouds into far Northeast OH and Northwest PA this 
morning, with a few showers into PA where moisture is a bit 
deeper. Locations west/southwest of roughly a Cleveland-Canton 
line will see a mostly sunny day. With the low-level ridge axis
not really pushing into Northeast OH/Northwest PA until this 
evening some lake effect clouds will continue flowing in for 
much of the day, with continued minor shower chances in 
Northwest PA. West-northwest winds will be a bit brisk, 
especially through early this afternoon. There will be another 
cold frontal passage on Tuesday, though it's expected to be a 
dry frontal passage with little airmass change. Highs in the 50s
with lows in the 30s/40s (largely above freezing) are expected
through Wednesday. Tuesday will be the warm day, when portions
of the area will likely get into the 60s. 

KEY MESSAGE 2... 
A notable pattern amplification is still on track for the end of
the week across the eastern U.S., bringing a return to more
notable precipitation chances and the chilliest airmass we've
seen so far this fall...and potentially some wet snowflakes. 

Ridging will amplify from the eastern slope of the Rockies
towards Hudson Bay starting on Wednesday, with a shortwave
expected to round the amplifying ridge and drop into the Great
Lakes and Ohio Valley Wednesday night and Thursday. This
shortwave will bring an injection of polar (not arctic) air 
into the eastern CONUS while interacting/phasing with another 
wave in the sub-tropical jet Thursday into Friday. This will 
lead to a large, deepening, slow-moving trough over the eastern 
U.S. and southeastern Canada late week into the weekend. Ridging
over the North Atlantic and a closed low near Newfoundland, 
often referred to as a -NAO, further supports a deep and slow- 
moving trough over the east that will be slow to exit. At the 
surface, a cold front is likely to cross the area late Wednesday
night or Thursday as developing low pressure tracks through the
Ohio Valley. This developing low pressure is expected to really
begin deepening near the Mid Atlantic coast Thursday night into
Friday. Chilly, moist cyclonic flow is expected to continue 
behind the low beneath troughing aloft through Saturday and 
into Sunday...there is improving agreement that surface ridging
will begin working in on Sunday but that the ridge axis won't 
really move into the local area until Sunday night or Monday. 

In terms of sensible weather, there are decent odds for rain
showers Wednesday night into Thursday as the front and
developing low move through the region. Behind this, an 
inverted trough axis is likely to extend towards the Great Lakes
beneath the deepening upper-level trough into Friday. This will
keep synoptic precip going, especially across eastern portions 
of the area. Synoptic precip is likely to shift east Friday 
night into the weekend, though some amount of north-northwest 
flow lake effect will continue and keep shower chances in the 
forecast south-southeast of the lake until the surface ridge 
axis works in Sunday night or Monday. Compared to prior runs, 
agreement among the non-GFS operational models and ensembles, 
including AI versions, has increased a bit. The GFS, with a much
stronger and slower surface low that amplifies west of the 
Appalachians, is an outlier, with most other guidance coming 
into better agreement on the general scenario laid out above,
with the low deepening well to our east but troughing
maintaining influence through the weekend. Still, the phasing 
of shortwaves and development of low pressure is something 
guidance struggles with, so will watch for any adjustments back 
towards a more amplified solution that could increase QPF
Thursday and Friday over the next few cycles. There's also 
improving agreement that some lake effect precip will continue 
through the weekend, though the impression is that precip 
should become more hit/miss and confined to areas downwind of
the lake this weekend as we gradually lose synoptic moisture. 

Am not expecting rain amounts or wind gusts to be especially 
impactful with this system though it will be wet, somewhat 
blustery, and generally unpleasant. The main talking point has 
been potential for some snow across the area, as it would be the
first of the season. It should be too warm for the synoptic 
precip to mix with snow through most of Thursday night. 850mb 
temperatures bottom out at -4 to -7C Friday and Saturday as 
deeper cold works in, with moderation starting on Sunday. 
Temperatures aloft can support snow by late Thursday night or 
Friday, though the low-levels will be "warmer" given the lack of
arctic influence and modification from the still-mild Great 
Lakes. Mainly rain is expected though wet snow or graupel may 
mix in at times, mainly away from the lake and during the
